Portland General Electric Company Second Revision of Sheet No. 109-1
P.U.C. Oregon No. E-19 Canceling First Revision of Sheet No. 109-1
SCHEDULE 109
ENERGY TRUST OF OREGON FUNDING ADJUSTMENT
PURPOSE
To fund the acquisition of Energy Efficiency as administered by the Energy Trust of Oregon (ETO)
for the benefit of the Company’s Customers pursuant to ORS 757.054.
AVAILABLE
In all territory served by the Company.
APPLICABLE
To all Residential and Nonresidential Customers located within the Company’s service territory.
Nonresidential Customers who meet the eligibility qualifications under 2021 Legislative Session
House Bill (HB) 3141 and whose load exceeded 1 aMW but less than 10 aMW during the prior
calendar year are subject to an annual cap of $250,000 for combined Energy Trust of Oregon
Funding Adjustment and Public Purpose Charges. Nonresidential Customers who meet the
eligibility qualifications under HB 3141 and whose load exceeded 10 aMW are subject to an
annual cap of $4,000,000 for combined Energy Trust of Oregon Funding Adjustment and Public
Purpose Charges.
Sites receiving service under Schedule 96 are charged such that these sites pay the maximum (N)
allowable amount under HB 3141 per Commission Order 26-154, directing treatment of large
loads under the POWER Act (HB 3546). (N)
SELF-DIRECTING CUSTOMER (SDC)
Pursuant to OAR 860-038-0480, to qualify to be an SDC, the Large Nonresidential Customer
must have a load that exceeds 1 aMW at a Site as defined in Rule B and receive certification from
the Oregon Department of Energy (ODOE) as an SDC. The Company will include the credits due,
as reported by the ODOE, to the applicable portions of the SDC’s monthly Schedule 109 Charge.
BALANCING ACCOUNT
The Company will maintain a balancing account to accrue the incremental amounts between the
amounts associated with the ETO budget and the revenues collected under this schedule. This
balancing account will accrue interest at the Commission-authorized rate for deferred accounts.
Advice No. 26-24
Issued June 3, 2026 Effective for service
Angelica Espinosa, Senior Vice President on and after July 8, 2026

SPECIAL CONDITION
1. Any adjustments relating to eligible Nonresidential Customers subject to annual caps as
described in HB 3141 will be paid from the Schedule 109 Energy Trust of Oregon Funding
Adjustment balancing account. Nonresidential Customers meeting the requirements for the
combined annual cap under HB 3141 will notify the Company by March 31 of the following
year to receive an adjustment.
TERM
This Schedule will terminate on January 1, 2036.
